{"id":"JMAP-kz4f","title":"Federation peer auth: no-I/O spec parts (RFC 9421 signing/verification)","description":"Per decision JMAP-vjm0: the spec-defined, I/O-free parts of draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00 §Peer Authentication Model (jmap-chat-spec 03985ef, L174-230) go in crate-jmap. Key fetching over HTTPS, DNSSEC/TXT lookups, key cache, refetch rate limit and replay store stay in the caller/support crate.

Scope (pure functions, clock and lookups passed in):
1. peerSigningKeys types: Ed25519 OKP JWK; RFC 7638 thumbprint; usable-key filter (kty OKP, crv Ed25519, recomputed thumbprint == kid, no private members -> ignore entry) (§Key Publication).
2. keyid format/parse '<peer-domain>#<kid>'.
3. Signing: build the RFC 9421 signature base and Signature-Input/Signature for @method, @target-uri, content-digest (when content), params tag=jmap-chat-peer, alg=ed25519, keyid, created, expires (<= created+300), nonce (>=128-bit CSPRNG, base64url). Private key supplied by the caller.
4. Verification checks 1-4 and 6 of §Request Signing: exactly one jmap-chat-peer signature, alg, covered components, keyid -> usable key, Ed25519 verify, clock window (60s skew, 300s lifetime), RFC 9530 sha-256 content-digest match. Check 5 (nonce replay) via a caller-supplied seen(domain, nonce) and a returned (domain, nonce, forget_after = expires+60s) to record. Result: authenticated peer domain or a typed rejection (all map to HTTP 403).
5. DNSSEC precedence (§DNSSEC Key Binding) as a pure fn over a caller-supplied validation result enum {Secure(kids), SecureDenial, Insecure, NoRecords, Indeterminate, LookupFailed, Bogus}: Secure with records filters keys to listed kids; Bogus rejects; all others use HTTPS keys alone. Parse 'v=jmappeer1; kid=<kid>' TXT values.
6. Identity-host binding rule (§identity-binding) as a pure predicate.

Open at start: placement (new crate e.g. crate-jmap-peer-auth vs feature-gated module of jmap-chat-server) and deps (ed25519 + sha2 needed; check crates.io for a maintained RFC 9421 crate and prefer a thin adapter, per JMAP-vjm0). No HTTP client, DNS, or persistence deps.","acceptance_criteria":"Tests use external oracles only: RFC 8037 App. A.3 Ed25519 JWK thumbprint (kPrK_qmxVWaYVA9wwBF6Iuo3vVzz7TxHCTwXBygrS4k, also the draft's keyid example); RFC 9421 App. B.2.6 ed25519 signature test vector; RFC 9530 sha-256 Content-Digest examples. Each verification check has a negative test quoting the draft rule. DNSSEC precedence covered for every enum case.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"feature","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-10-19T21:15:10.94268999Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-10-19T21:15:10.94268999Z","dependencies":[{"issue_id":"JMAP-kz4f","depends_on_id":"JMAP-5qez","type":"blocks","created_at":"2026-10-19T21:15:11.32289497Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}
new_value: {"notes":"2026-10-19: with support crates now in this workspace (JMAP-vjm0 amended), placement option: one peer-auth crate holding these pure parts with the I/O half (JMAP-atfj) behind a feature, so jmap-chat-server can depend on the pure part without HTTP/DNS deps. Decide at start."}
